name: Discount excluded from value — the conditions that separate a discount given before or at supply from one given after
definition: Section 15(3) excludes a discount from the value of supply on two mutually exclusive routes, and each route has its own conditions. ROUTE A, s.15(3)(a) — the discount is given before or at the time of the supply, AND has been duly recorded in the invoice issued in respect of such supply. ROUTE B, s.15(3)(b) — the discount is given after the supply has been effected, and BOTH of two conditions hold: (i) the discount is established in terms of an agreement entered into at or before the time of such supply AND is specifically linked to relevant invoices, and (ii) the input tax credit attributable to the discount, on the basis of a document issued by the supplier, has been reversed by the recipient. A discount that satisfies neither route does not reduce the value of supply.
why_it_exists: A discount is the one adjustment a business makes constantly and documents loosely. Section 15(3) is where the law converts 'we gave them a rebate' into a testable set of facts. The post-supply route is a CHAIN: timing of the agreement, linkage to specific invoices, and the recipient's credit reversal. Drop any one link and the value of the supply is unchanged — which means the credit note reduces the books and not the tax, and the difference is an understatement of output tax.
inputs: whether the discount was given before or at the time of the supply, or after the supply was effected
ROUTE A — whether the discount is duly recorded in the invoice issued in respect of such supply
ROUTE B condition (i) — whether the discount is established in terms of an agreement entered into at or before the time of such supply
ROUTE B condition (i) — whether the discount is specifically linked to relevant invoices
ROUTE B condition (ii) — whether the supplier has issued a document on the basis of which the credit is reversed
ROUTE B condition (ii) — whether the recipient has reversed the input tax credit attributable to the discount
outputs: the discount is excluded from the value under ROUTE A
or the discount is excluded from the value under ROUTE B
or the discount is NOT excluded, naming the specific condition that failed
preconditions: a value of supply exists to which the discount would otherwise attach
the supply to which the discount relates is identified — ROUTE A ties the discount to the invoice for that supply, ROUTE B ties it to relevant invoices
exceptions: ROUTE A CONDITION — recorded in the invoice: a pre-supply discount not recorded in the invoice is not excluded by s.15(3)(a)
ROUTE B CONDITION 1 — agreement timing: the agreement must have been entered into AT OR BEFORE the time of the supply; an agreement made afterwards fails
ROUTE B CONDITION 2 — invoice linkage: the discount must be specifically linked to relevant invoices; a lump-sum rebate over a period with no invoice linkage fails
ROUTE B CONDITION 3 — supplier's document: the reversal must be on the basis of a document issued by the supplier
ROUTE B CONDITION 4 — recipient's reversal: the input tax credit attributable to the discount must have been reversed BY THE RECIPIENT; the supplier cannot satisfy this condition by his own act
ROUTE B conditions (i) and (ii) are joined by 'and' — they are cumulative, never alternatives

common_mistakes: reducing the taxable value by a post-supply discount as soon as the credit note is issued, before the recipient has reversed the attributable credit
treating the four ROUTE B conditions as a general test of commercial reasonableness rather than four separate facts, each of which must be evidenced
excluding a pre-supply discount that was agreed but never recorded in the invoice — ROUTE A requires the invoice record
reading 'established in terms of an agreement entered into at or before the time of such supply' as satisfied by a long-standing trading practice with no agreement
treating a year-end volume rebate as automatically excludable — it typically fails invoice linkage as well as agreement timing
assuming that because the discount is genuine and the credit note is valid, the value must fall — s.15(3) is the only route, and it is conditional
confusing the accounting treatment with the valuation treatment — a discount can reduce revenue in the books and leave the value of supply untouched

evidence_required: the invoice, for ROUTE A — the discount must be visible on it
the agreement, dated, for ROUTE B condition (i) — and the date must be at or before the time of supply
the schedule linking the discount to specific invoices, for ROUTE B condition (i)
the document issued by the supplier on the basis of which the credit is reversed, for ROUTE B condition (ii)
evidence from the recipient that the attributable input tax credit has been reversed, for ROUTE B condition (ii)
confidence_factors: zero for a post-supply discount until the recipient's input tax credit reversal is evidenced — this fact lives in a third party's records and cannot be inferred from the supplier's own
zero where the agreement is undated or its date cannot be established relative to the time of supply
weak where the discount is stated as a percentage over a period rather than linked to identified invoices
weak for ROUTE A where the invoice shows a net figure but no discount line, because 'duly recorded in the invoice' is then unproven
the time of supply is a separate determination — confidence in ROUTE B condition (i) can be no stronger than confidence in the time of supply it is measured against
validation_checks: the route is decided first — before or at the time of supply, or after — and recorded
for ROUTE A: the discount appears in the invoice issued in respect of that supply
for ROUTE B: the agreement exists AND its date is at or before the time of supply
for ROUTE B: the discount is linked to identified invoices, not to a period or a turnover band alone
for ROUTE B: a document issued by the supplier exists as the basis of the reversal
for ROUTE B: the recipient's reversal of the attributable input tax credit is evidenced before the value is reduced
a discount failing any condition leaves the value of supply UNCHANGED, and that outcome is recorded rather than treated as an omission
examples: a discount agreed before the supply and shown on the face of the invoice — excluded under s.15(3)(a)

a quarterly discount fixed in a dated distribution agreement signed before the supplies, applied against listed invoice numbers, with the recipient's credit reversal evidenced — all ROUTE B conditions met, excluded under s.15(3)(b)
counterexamples: a year-end volume rebate issued by credit note where no pre-supply agreement exists — ROUTE B condition (i) fails, the value of supply is unchanged and the rebate does not reduce the GST

a rebate under a valid pre-supply agreement, linked to invoices, where the recipient has not reversed the attributable credit — ROUTE B condition (ii) fails, so the value of supply is unchanged even though every other condition holds

a discount negotiated before supply but recorded only in a separate letter and not in the invoice — ROUTE A fails; and because the discount was given before the supply, ROUTE B is not available either
